clue.text: Bunk where youth has solitary confinement

indicators.note: the youth has the solitary one held within him, so one word sits inside the other
solitary confinement here signals that the word for solitary is shut up inside the youth

parts.note: a boy is a youth
lone means solitary

explanation.surface: A cynic dismisses the idea that a young offender is put in solitary confinement as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solitary confinement' reads as one prison phrase, but 'has' and 'confinement' split it: the youth holds the solitary word inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for nonsense or rubbish talk, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Part of a dress cut into pieces — that's beyond a stinker!

indicators.note: the word for cutting up comes beyond, after, the stinker

parts.note: BO, body odour, is a stink
to dice is to cut into small pieces

explanation.surface: A dress slashed to shreds smells worse than anything imaginable.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the upper section of a woman's dress, above the waist.

clue.text: Continue trailing around duck in pool?

indicators.note: the trailing and continuing words wrap around the duck

parts.note: to lag is to trail behind
on is a call to continue, as in carry on
a duck is a score of nil in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A duck keeps paddling around behind in a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird on the pool but is nought, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of salt water separated from the sea, a kind of pool, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Flash Gordon's last feature overcoming criminal, poster claims

indicators.note: the last letter of Gordon is taken
the poster claims, or takes in, the feature and criminal

parts.note: an ad is a poster advertising something

indicators.note: in a down clue the facial feature sits over the criminal

parts.note: a nose is a facial feature
a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A poster for Flash Gordon shows the hero beating a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash Gordon' seems a single name, but 'Flash' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash is an instant, and a billionth of a second is an extremely brief moment.

clue.text: Having removed hat, policeman climbs over top of outbuilding to get hooligan

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters read upwards, backwards
the bareheaded policeman goes over, covering, the top letter
the policeman's word loses its first letter, its hat

parts.note: a bobby is a British police officer

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A copper takes off his helmet and clambers over a shed roof to catch a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: BOBBY without hat gives OBBY; it takes O to make OBBOY, which 'climbs' upward to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobbo is British slang for a loutish, aggressive young man, a hooligan.

clue.text: Sense of dread in oligarch's heart, as a hoodlum

indicators.note: the dread is placed in the middle letters of the oligarch, sitting between them
the heart of a word is its central letters, here the two middle ones of oligarch

parts.note: angst is a feeling of dread or anxiety

explanation.surface: An oligarch secretly fears that, deep down, he is nothing more than a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' of an eight-letter word is its middle pair of letters, not a single one.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangsta is slang for a gang member or street criminal, which is a kind of hoodlum.

clue.text: Gradual line oddly askew, coming from the thyroid, perhaps

indicators.note: askew means skewed out of position, so the letters are rearranged
the odd letters of line are taken, first and third

explanation.surface: A slow, slightly crooked line on a scan suggests a thyroid problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The thyroid is a gland, so anything from it relates to glands; perhaps signals an example.

clue.text: Less than ten, I need?

indicators.note: the hidden word is less than all the letters of the phrase, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Someone wants fewer than ten of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is the number just below ten, so it is less than ten, as the whole clue says.

clue.text: Satirical pieces about god in tight clothing

indicators.note: the satirical pieces go about, around, the god

parts.note: skits are short satirical sketches
Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: Comic sketches mock a deity squeezed into figure-hugging garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are close-fitting stretch trousers, a tight garment.

clue.text: Singer gathering support for Australian city

indicators.note: the singer gathers in, encloses, the support

parts.note: Adele is the English pop singer
aid means support

explanation.surface: A singer draws backing for a concert in an Australian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia.

clue.text: Eat half of plate, then drink

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for plate is taken, its opening two letters

parts.note: a dish is a plate
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A diner eats half of what is on the plate and then has a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig in is an idiom for starting to eat heartily.

clue.text: Sauce, if horse growls? Then ___, did you say?

indicators.note: asking whether you said it means the spoken form of the phrase is wanted

parts.note: if a horse can growl like a bear, then the swap is that a bear neighs, giving the words bear neighs

explanation.surface: A silly riddle: if horses growled, bears would presumably neigh instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank with the absurd consequence, BEAR NEIGHS; spoken, it matches the name of the French sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearnaise is a classic French sauce of butter, egg yolk, shallots and tarragon.

clue.text: Those exchanged in an argument for these

definitions.meaning: angry remarks traded in a quarrel
the puzzles the solver is doing right now

explanation.surface: Remarks traded in a row are set against the puzzles in front of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these' refers to the puzzles themselves: the clue points at the very thing you are solving.
explanation.definitionFit: Angry words are cross words; the self-referring 'these' means the puzzles in the newspaper.

clue.text: Trojan prince is lacking a jumper

indicators.note: the prince's name is lacking the two letters of the word is

parts.note: Paris was the prince of Troy who abducted Helen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A legendary prince of Troy turns out to be missing his sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' tempts as the British word for a sweater; it is a parachutist.
explanation.definitionFit: A para is a paratrooper, a soldier who jumps from aircraft by parachute.

clue.text: Sport takes off, given topping coverage

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are given a covering of the cake topping, sitting inside it

parts.note: icing is a covering topping on a cake

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are off, disordered, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A sport becomes popular and gets lots of top-level media coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes off' looks like 'becomes popular', but 'off' is the anagram signal for the word before it, and 'given' puts the result inside the cake covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice skating is a sport, competitive in figure and speed forms.

clue.text: Tom has followed instructions, when about to get involved

indicators.note: the word for following instructions goes about, that is around, the tom

parts.note: complied means did as instructed
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A tomcat has, unusually, done as it was told, just as things were about to get messy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' reads as a man's name, but it is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Involved and complicated are synonyms, both meaning intricate or hard to follow.

clue.text: Union with club's splintered fragments

parts.note: a match is a union, as in a marriage
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A trade union and a club both shatter into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchwood is wood broken into tiny splinters, as in smashed to matchwood.

clue.text: Expert not entirely comprehending opera that's weird

indicators.note: comprehending means taking in, so the trimmed word encloses the opera
only part of the word for expert is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: able means skilled, expert
Norma is an opera by Bellini

explanation.surface: A specialist who only half understands an opera finds it strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal and weird both mean departing from what is usual.

clue.text: Island retail giant?

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre, a place for retail
an orca, or killer whale, is a giant of the sea

explanation.surface: A huge chain store is pictured; read as two words, it becomes a whale in a shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retail giant' reads as a big store chain, but splits into a shopping place and a huge whale.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallorca is the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Mental aberrations, opposite points written in biro, smart perhaps?

indicators.note: the compass letters are written into the rearranged pen-and-smart letters
perhaps suggests these letters are a possible version, a new arrangement of them

parts.note: north and south, N and S, are opposite points of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a smart pen with compass points written on it might count as madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the pen and smart letters together; 'written in' places the two compass points inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainstorm can mean a sudden fit of mental confusion, a momentary lapse of reason.

clue.text: A zebra dropping guts, munching bitter plant

indicators.note: the gutted zebra munches the beer, holding it inside
dropping its guts leaves only the outer letters of zebra

parts.note: bitter is a type of ale, a British beer

explanation.surface: A zebra being disembowelled while chewing on a sour plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' is a British pale ale, not a taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The azalea is a flowering shrub related to the rhododendron.

clue.text: Shrivelled old man secreting foundation in exquisite set of personal make-up?

indicators.note: the old man secretes, hides within him, the letter

parts.note: a gnome is a wizened little old man of folklore

indicators.note: in a down clue the foundation is the bottom, the final letter

explanation.surface: A wrinkled old man hides exquisite foundation in his make-up kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foundation' and 'make-up' suggest cosmetics; foundation is the bottom letter, and make-up is one's genetic make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A genome is the complete set of an organism's genes, its personal genetic constitution.

clue.text: All leaders in organisation invariably like you, overly suave

indicators.note: the leaders of the four words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Everyone in charge of the company is, without fail, just like you: far too smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: An oily manner is unctuous and ingratiating, smooth to an excessive degree.

clue.text: Knuckle-dragger in German war machine almost infiltrating ring

indicators.note: the war machine, cut short, infiltrates the word for ring, entering it

parts.note: to chime is to ring

indicators.note: almost the whole tank word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a Panzer is a German tank

explanation.surface: A brutish thug inside a German tank closes in on a ring of enemies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knuckle-dragger' reads as an insult for a lout but is here literal: an ape that walks on its knuckles.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimpanzees walk on all fours on their knuckles, so the slang insult fits them literally.

clue.text: Unfortunate bosom?

indicators.note: an unfortunate arrangement of letters means they are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A sorry chest is lamented.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for fatty male breasts, an unfortunate chest for a man.

clue.text: A choice of extremes in perversion?

definitions.text: A choice of extremes in perversion?

indicators.note: the choice word sits between, made of, the two extreme letters
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: or is the word that offers a choice

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what selection of extreme material perverts would make.
explanation.definitionFit: Pornography is the obvious choice of extreme material for the perverted, as the whole clue suggests.

clue.text: Bringing over old stuff from the East, game for Venetian traveller

indicators.note: bringing the two pieces over turns them round, read the other way
in an across clue reading from the east means right to left, backwards

parts.note: to cram is to stuff
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: Someone imports antiques from the Orient, then plays a match, like an explorer of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the thirteenth-century merchant from Venice who journeyed to China.

clue.text: Entrance blocked to vast throne room in northern residence

indicators.note: the word for vast loses its entrance, its first letter

parts.note: big means vast
humorously, the throne is the toilet, so a throne room is a loo, British slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: Access to a vast royal throne room in a northern palace has been barred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throne room' suggests a palace, but the throne is a jokey word for the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a snow house built by Inuit peoples of the Arctic north.

clue.text: Scholarly head of languages brought in

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: earned means brought in, as money

explanation.surface: The chief of the languages department has been recruited.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned (two syllables) describes someone erudite, with much academic knowledge.

clue.text: Indications show surprising gains, for example, after recovery

indicators.note: the turned example comes after the shuffled gains
surprising suggests the letters of gains are jolted into a new order
recovery read as re-covering, going back over, turns the abbreviation round

explanation.surface: Figures show unexpected gains, perhaps, following an economic recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprising' shuffles GAINS into SIGNA; 'recovery' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Signage is the collective set of signs that indicate directions or information.
